title: Flat separated algebraic-space isomorphism over a dense open is an open immersion
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $g:Y\to T$ be a separated, flat, locally finite-type morphism. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, meaning that every affine etale scheme chart of $T$ has quasi-compact inverse image of $V$. Suppose $Y\times_TV\to V$ is an isomorphism and $V$ is schematically dense in $T$: the restriction map $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ of sheaves on the small etale site is injective. Then $g$ is an open immersion. No quasi-compactness of $g$ or of $T$, and no properness of $g$, are required.

proof.text: The restriction $g_V:Y\times_TV\to V$ is an isomorphism, hence locally of finite presentation: for compatible etale scheme charts $a:U'\to Y_V$, $b:U\to V$ and $h:U'\to U$ with $g_Va=bh$, both $U'\to V$ and $U\to V$ are etale, so $h$ is a morphism over $V$ between etale objects and is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; as a scheme morphism it is therefore locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-finite-presentation-dense-open] with $X=Y$, base $T$, and the given open $V$. Its flatness, local finite type, quasi-compactness of $V\to T$, schematic density and local finite presentation over $V$ hypotheses all hold. Thus $g$ is locally of finite presentation.

Put $P=Y\times_TY$ with first projection $p_1:P\to Y$. This is a base change of the flat morphism $g$, so it is flat by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-pullback-schematic-density] first to $g$ and $V\subset T$: $Y_V\subset Y$ is a quasi-compact schematically dense open. Apply it again to $p_1$ and $Y_V\subset Y$. It gives a quasi-compact schematically dense open $W=p_1^{-1}(Y_V)=P\times_TV\subset P$. These identifications follow on each test scheme by writing a point of $P$ as a pair with equal images in $T$.

Separatedness says that $\Delta_g:Y\hookrightarrow P$ is a closed immersion. Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_P$ be its ideal, using [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence]. Over $W=P_V$, the diagonal is the diagonal of the isomorphism $g_V$, hence is an isomorphism. Therefore $\mathcal I|_W=0$. The map $\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_P\to j_{W*}\mathcal O_W$ is zero, while $\mathcal O_P\to j_{W*}\mathcal O_W$ is injective by step 2. Consequently $\mathcal I=0$, and the ideal correspondence identifies $\Delta_g$ with the whole of $P$. Thus $\Delta_g$ is an isomorphism. For each scheme $H$, a pair $a,b\in Y(H)$ with $g(a)=g(b)$ is a point of $P(H)$ and is uniquely of the form $(c,c)$; hence $a=b$. This proves that $g$ is a monomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-monomorphism-representable] to the flat morphism $g$, now a monomorphism by step 3. It follows that $Y\times_T H$ is a scheme for every scheme $H\to T$.

Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to T$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By step 4, $Y_U=Y\times_TU$ is a scheme. The projection $Y_U\to Y$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Consequently the compatible etale scheme charts $Y_U\to Y$ and $U\to T$ test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] directly: $g_U:Y_U\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is a monomorphism, since two pairs over any test scheme with equal projections to $U$ have equal $Y$ components by step 3. Apply the scheme Mathlib leaf [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open] to conclude $g_U$ is an open immersion. The target-local criterion [lem-trf-space-open-immersion-etale-local] now gives that $g$ is an open immersion.
